main_text.p: scripturæ s. repugnantia, nō est audiendus magistratus politicus; imò verò etiā viros principes monere, castigare & corrigere decet, ad imitationem prophetarum & aliorum fidorum dei servorum. nam semper oportet Deo magis obedire, quàm hominibus.

II. Impium esse, vel sanè rem plenam periculi, deferre magistratui tantam potentiam in ecclesiâ, quantam habet in politiâ. Resp. Neque hoc fit ab orthodoxis doctoribus: plus enim potest in politicis quàm in ecclesiasticis. In politiâ potest novas leges ferre, & subditos etiâ invitos ad illas observandas cogere: at in ecclesiâ non potest novos fidei articulos condere, neque potest subditos suos ad illorum observationem per vim adigere. 12 Ita actum esse de ecclesiâ, & aperiri ianuam tyrannicis ingeniis saeviendi in subditorum conscientias. Resp. Si magistratus non cedat locū sanis consiliis, & ad verbi divini praescriptum instituat in religionis negocio, non tenen-

page.notes: Long s read as plain s throughout. The opening "f." in the first line is printed as an abbreviation, transcribed as "s." (scripturæ s.), reading uncertain because the long s is close to f. The "12" before "Ita" is a thesis number inside the paragraph, kept as printed. The word "tenen-" is the catchword at the foot right; the text ends with the full line "instituat in religionis negocio, non". Left margin strip is the neighbouring page and was left out.
